newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador launches drive against fiscal deficit.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador launches drive against fiscal deficit.

text.p: Ecuadoran care-taker President Fabian Alarcon announced on Friday a range of economic measures with emphasis in the fight against fiscal deficit.
In a speech to the nation he also said his government expected the economy to grow 3.5 percent this year and four percent next year.
"Our government's priority is to cut the fiscal deficit at the least social cost," said Alarcon, who was named by the Congress as interim president for a year and a half this month.
Alarcon said the government would make a big effort to trim the fiscal deficit this year to 2.5 percent from 6.6 percent of gross domestic product, which was estimated at $1.3 billion.
He also said he expected to reduce inflation to between 20 and 23 percent in 1998 from 26 percent in 1996. He did not give figures for 1997.
Public expenditure would be reduced by 10 percent or $400 million, said Alarcon. He promised the country would honour its $14.5 billion external debt.
The crawling peg policy introduced in 1994 would be maintained.
Import fees will be increased by four percent except those covered by free trade agreements. Electricty fees will by cut by 50 percent.
The previous government of President Abadala Bucaram, removed in February by the Congress on grounds of "mental incapacity", made big increases in all prices of public services.
Alarcon reaffirmed that Ecuador will not apply the convertibility plan Bucaram wanted to impose under the guidance of former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo.
The plan involved pegging the value of the local sucre currency to the dollar.
The public fees hike and his plans to apply convertibility, together with an eccentric personality are widely considered the reasons behind Bucaram's dismissal.
